messages:
mike: Hey team — private VPC customer hitting intermittent 403s when the on-prem installer pulls models from our registry. They say it works from other networks. Asking for minimal egress allowlist (hosts/ports) and any TLS/SNI gotchas to share with their infra team.

jess: Can you paste a quick repro (curl + dns dig) and any error text? 403 usually means auth but could be SNI/host mismatch behind ALB.

mike: Repro we captured from their bastion:

curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest
*   Trying 18.205.93.45:443...
* Connected to registry.redwood.ai (18.205.93.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
> GET /api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest HTTP/1.1
> Host: registry.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.83.1
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> 
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: 01FZXY...
< date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 16:34:22 GMT

Response body: {"error":"access_denied","detail":"token valid but access denied to model shard host 3"}

Also tried `openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai` — cert chain OK, no obvious handshake errors.

They have split-horizon DNS: internal resolves registry.redwood.ai -> 10.2.1.12 (NAT gw then egress) and external resolves to public IP. Noticed when they curl using --resolve to force public IP it works. When internal resolves to private IP they sometimes get 403.

jess: Interesting — that smells like either: 1) the SNI the ALB expects doesn't match the hostname seen at TLS termination because of TLS passthrough vs. termination, or 2) a proxy in path is replacing host header or stripping SNI. Since openssl s_client with -servername succeeded, maybe downstream LB expects external IP in request path for routing to correct shard.

Try reproducer to force SNI mismatch:

# force direct ip but keep Host header (should still work)
curl -v --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:10.2.1.12 \
  -H 'Host: registry.redwood.ai' \
  https://registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest
\nIf that fails, try `--resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:18.205.93.45` to force public IP.

olga: Also check whether their NAT GW is using an egress IP that we have allowlisted for their org. If they are behind corporate proxy that injects/terminates TLS (MITM) then token auth may be failing because we verify cert pinning for some model shard hosts. Do we have any pinned certs for shards?

infra-bot: Quick checklist from infra: please confirm the following for minimal egress allowlist: list of hostnames, DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to public resolvers or do they use DoT/DoH (853/443), outbound TCP 443 to hosts below, OCSP responder access for certificate validation, and access to our auth and telemetry endpoints. We also need their NAT egress IP(s) if they want inbound allowlisting on our side.

jess: I'll assemble a minimal host list — posting draft that addresses their installer + runtime telemetry + auth + model pulls. Note: we avoid listing broad aws IP ranges and prefer hostnames (SNI/ALB requires hostname).

Draft minimal hostnames (tcp/443 unless noted):
- registry.redwood.ai  (model registry API + shard redirectors)
- shard-*.model-registry.storage.redwood.ai  (object store for model shards; wildcard)
- auth.redwood.ai  (oauth token endpoints / token refresh)
- telemetry.redwood.ai  (stats + usage pings)
- ocsp.redwood.ai  (OCSP responder)
- files.pythonhosted.org  (pip wheels)
- pypi.org  (pip index)
- artifactory.cdn.redwood.ai  (internal package artifacts)
- s3.amazonaws.com and *.s3.amazonaws.com (if installer pulls from S3)
- sts.amazonaws.com and kms.<region>.amazonaws.com (if using AWS auth)

Needed ports / protocols:
- TCP 443 outbound to all hosts above
- UDP 53 / TCP 53 to their DNS resolver (or TCP 853 if using DoT)
- TCP 443 to OCSP/CRL endpoints (certificate revocation checks)

Security/TLS notes to pass on to customer:
- Do NOT terminate TLS on corporate proxy unless you can preserve the original Host/SNI and pass-through Authorization headers intact. Our auth tokens are bearer tokens validated against expected shard-host pairs.
- If using split-horizon, ensure internal DNS resolves to an IP that preserves the same SNI/host routing that public DNS uses. For ALBs our routing depends on Host + SNI.
- If they see intermittent 403s, check for a proxy that does TLS re-write per-request (could rotate client IPs or headers).
- If they use DoH/DoT to nonstandard resolvers, ensure OCSP lookups can reach ocsp.redwood.ai.

mike: Thanks. I also captured tcpdump when 403 happens — saw SYN -> TLS -> HTTP 403 (no 401 challenge). They also reported sometimes a 502 Gateway depending on which shard redirects. Will share pcap privately.

olga: Can they try adding a temporary /etc/hosts entry mapping registry.redwood.ai to public IP (e.g., 18.205.93.45) just to prove it's DNS/egress path related? If that makes it stable, we know it's split-horizon or proxy issue.

mike: They tried that — forcing public IP made it succeed consistently. So I think it's a proxy/NAT path difference. They asked for a one-page kb to hand to their networking team with minimal list & repro steps.

jess: I'll post a short KB snippet they can hand to infra + a proposed allowlist table (hosts + ports + purpose) and a bullet list of repro commands.

KB snippet (copyable):
1) Allow outbound TCP/443 to these hostnames: registry.redwood.ai, auth.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.org, shard-*.model-registry.storage.redwood.ai, artifactory.cdn.redwood.ai, s3.amazonaws.com, sts.amazonaws.com, kms.<region>.amazonaws.com
2) Ensure DNS (UDP/TCP 53 or DoT 853/DoH 443) can resolve public names for those hosts; do not rewrite Host headers.
3) Ensure TLS SNI is preserved across any corporate proxy/NGFW. If you must terminate TLS, configure passthrough for these hostnames.
4) If you use egress IP allowlisting on our side, provide NAT egress IP(s) so we can verify and whitelist from our side.

Repro commands to run from client network: (replace PUBLIC_IP below with registry public IP)
- curl -v https://registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- curl -v --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:PUBLIC_IP https://registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models/abcd1234/manifest
- openssl s_client -connect registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.redwood.ai
- dig registry.redwood.ai +short # check split-horizon

infra-bot: I've filed INFRA-2748 to validate our ALB routing and check whether any shard-hosts perform geofencing by source IP. Also requested the team to sanity-check OCSP responder reachability and whether we can accept connections from their egress IPs.

oncall: tagging infra + security for awareness. If customer wants expedited whitelist on our side provide NAT IPs and we'll fast-track a devops review. :rocket:

mike: Perfect — I'll send KB and their NAT IPs. ETA request from customer for whitelist? They asked for ETA within 24h if we can confirm host/port list and whether any cert pinning will block their proxy.

jess: We'll aim to respond within 24h. If they can share a pcap and NAT IPs now that helps. :thumbsup:
